## Upstream changes 1.18.0 -> 1.19.0

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — the upgrade requires Docker Compose ≥2.35.0 on the host and manual tracing-queue/config handling during rollout; no companion-service version mismatch applies since the Agent Backend doesn't depend on an unpinned engine, but config file layout and queue changes need operator action before/after applying.

### Breaking changes
- **Docker Compose version floor raised.** "Docker Compose now requires v2.35.0 or later" and "This is the minimum supported version for root `.env` overrides to take precedence when Compose resolves service defaults." An older Compose binary on the host will resolve env precedence incorrectly.
- **Tracing queue change.** "New tasks default to `OPS_TRACE_QUEUE=ops_trace_v2`. API, workers, and Beat must agree." The old queue-related variables are removed: "The old `OPS_TRACE_UNIFIED_ENABLED`, `OPS_TRACE_RETRYABLE_DISPATCH_MAX_RETRIES`, `OPS_TRACE_RETRYABLE_DISPATCH_DELAY_SECONDS`, and `OPS_TRACE_PARENT_CONTEXT_TTL_SECONDS` settings are removed." This template does not set `CELERY_QUEUES`/`CELERY_WORKER_QUEUES` explicitly, so a clean cut from 1.18.0 to 1.19.0 (not a rolling upgrade) should be unaffected, but the notes warn "Do not purge the old queue or ask the new retired handler to export legacy messages" for mixed-version rollouts.
- **Tracing config endpoint contract change.** "Custom clients of `GET /console/api/apps/{app_id}/trace-config` must consume `configured_secrets` instead of expecting saved secret values." Only relevant if the operator has custom tooling against this endpoint.
- **App package format v2 default.** "All Dify app exports now use package format v2... See the upgrade guide before importing new packages into older installations." Not a concern for same-stack upgrades but matters if exporting for use elsewhere.
- **Database migration chain.** "Upgrading from 1.18.0 applies six migration revisions, ending at `53c10126d551`." Includes a destructive dedup step: "Tracing configuration uniqueness (`53c10126d551`)... Superseded rows are deleted; downgrading the index does not restore them. Retain a database backup."

### Variables
- `OPS_TRACE_QUEUE` — new, defaults to `ops_trace_v2`. Not present in this compose/.env.example; will use upstream default.
- `OPS_TRACE_EXPORT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` — new, defaults to `6`.
- `ENABLE_TRACE_PAYLOAD_SWEEP_TASK` — new, defaults to `true`.
- `APP_PACKAGE_MAX_WORKFLOW_TOOLS` — new, defaults to `20`.
- `GUNICORN_KEEP_ALIVE` — new, defaults to `10` seconds.
- Removed: `OPS_TRACE_UNIFIED_ENABLED`, `OPS_TRACE_RETRYABLE_DISPATCH_MAX_RETRIES`, `OPS_TRACE_RETRYABLE_DISPATCH_DELAY_SECONDS`, `OPS_TRACE_PARENT_CONTEXT_TTL_SECONDS` — none of these appear in the template's `.env.example`, so nothing to clean up there.
- None of these are referenced in the compose file's `x-app-env` block or `.env.example`; they will take upstream defaults unless added.

### Data and dependencies
- Companion services (Postgres, Redis, Weaviate) are pinned in this compose file at 15-alpine, 7.4-alpine, and 1.27.0 respectively; the 1.19.0 notes name no required version change for any of them, so no mismatch is introduced by this range.
- Six migration revisions apply, ending at `53c10126d551`; `MIGRATION_ENABLED=true` is already the template's default so this runs automatically on `api` startup.
- Storage-cleanup index migration (`d7e9a1c3f502`) builds concurrently on Postgres but "still scans data and consumes I/O" — expect elevated load during startup on larger installs.
- Tracing dedup migration deletes superseded rows irreversibly — back up the database first.
- Extraction fixes for EPUB/EML/DOCX/CSV/Markdown/Notion only affect newly processed content: "Re-import or re-index documents whose stored content was affected."

### Before applying
- Confirm the host's Docker Compose is ≥2.35.0: `docker compose version`. This template's compose file requires it for correct `.env` override precedence going forward.
- Back up the database before upgrading, per the notes, given the irreversible tracing-config dedup migration.
- Bump the pinned versions together: `DIFY_API_IMAGE_VERSION`, `DIFY_WEB_IMAGE_VERSION`, `DIFY_LOCAL_SANDBOX_IMAGE_VERSION`, and `DIFY_AGENT_BACKEND_IMAGE_VERSION` all to `1.19.0` — the notes say "Use matching `1.19.0` API, worker, web, Agent Backend, and Local sandbox images." This template's `x-images` block pins all of these together; update the compose file's digests, not just `.env`.
- The plugin daemon moves to `0.6.14-local` per the notes ("The bundled plugin daemon is upgraded to 0.6.14-local") but the compose file's `plugin-daemon` default is still `0.6.10-local`. This requires updating `DIFY_PLUGIN_DAEMON_IMAGE_VERSION` (or the compose default) to match; the template's `.env.example` also still lists `DIFY_PLUGIN_DAEMON_IMAGE_VERSION=0.6.10-local` as its documented default.
- Keep `MIGRATION_ENABLED=true` (already the template default) through the restart so the six migrations apply.
- This is a single-stack, non-rolling deployment (one `api`, one `worker`, one `worker_beat`), so the tracing-queue rolling-upgrade sequencing in step 6 of the upgrade guide does not apply — a straight `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` carries the queue rename safely since there's no old/new consumer overlap to manage.
- No `PASSWORD_PEPPER` is configured by this template; nothing to preserve there.

## WHAT THE IMAGES THEMSELVES DIFFER IN

- `COMMIT_SHA`, `PYTHON_SHA256`: build provenance only, not actionable.
- `PYTHON_VERSION`: `3.13.17` -> `3.13.18` — patch-level Python bump inside the image, no host action needed.
- `UV_VERSION`: `0.8.9` -> `0.13.4` — matches the notes' mention of "Docker build tooling updates uv to 0.13.4," build-time only, no runtime effect.

These are internal build details and do not touch user, entrypoint, command, ports, volumes, healthcheck, or environment contracts the compose file relies on. Nothing here overrides or contradicts the notes for this image.

### Notes read
- Release notes for `1.19.0` (full body, including Upgrade guide, Detailed changes, and Environment variables sections).
- Baseline release notes for `1.18.0` (read only to confirm which requirements were already in force — e.g. `PASSWORD_PEPPER`, Python 3.13, Agent sandbox token — none of which are new in this range).
